questions.q: What does the underscore (`_;`) inside a modifier actually represent?
options: A placeholder marking where the rest of the function's body runs
A syntax error that must be removed
The function's return value
The modifier's name
questions.explain: The underscore tells Solidity exactly where, within the modifier, the actual function body should execute — everything before it runs first.

questions.q: What does the real `onlyOwner` modifier check before letting a function run?
options: That msg.sender equals the stored owner address
That the function has never been called before
That the contract has enough ETH balance
That the caller is using a specific compiler version
questions.explain: onlyOwner uses require(msg.sender == owner, "Not the owner") to block anyone except the recorded owner from proceeding.

questions.q: Why is a modifier better than copy-pasting the same require check into five different functions?
options: It keeps the logic in exactly one place, so it's easier to maintain and less error-prone
Modifiers run faster than require statements
Modifiers are the only way to use require at all
There's no real benefit — they're functionally identical
questions.explain: A modifier centralizes the check in one reusable place instead of duplicating the same require logic across every function that needs it.

questions.q: Can a real Solidity modifier take its own parameters, like the `costs(uint amount)` example?
options: Yes — a modifier can accept arguments just like a function
No — modifiers can never take any input
Only if the modifier is also marked public
Only inside a constructor
questions.explain: The costs modifier takes a real parameter (amount) and uses it in its own require check — modifiers can be parameterized just like functions.

questions.q: What happens when you apply two modifiers to the same function, like `onlyOwner whenNotPaused`?
options: Each modifier runs in order before the function's own body executes
Only the first modifier listed actually runs
This causes a guaranteed compile error
The modifiers run simultaneously in parallel
questions.explain: Stacked modifiers run in the order they're listed, each performing its own check, before the function body itself finally executes.
